# Founder Offer

An offer architect. The skill lists every problem a buyer hits on the way to the result they want (aiming for 15 to 30, pulled first from the buyer panel objections and the competitor complaints), turns each problem into a solution, scores each solution on value to the buyer and cost to deliver from the CFO numbers, and keeps the high-value, low-cost ones. It stacks what is left into the core offer described by its outcome, two or three bonuses that each kill one specific objection, a guarantee whose cost is modelled before it is promised, urgency or scarcity only when they are true, and a clear name for the offer. It scores the stack on the value equation (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time, effort) before and after, writes the new offer into the pitch, and re-tests it on a quick buyer panel with the same seed, reporting the buy rate before and after. Its method is the Offers lens in the sibling founder-board skill, a summary of the framework in $100M Offers by Alex Hormozi, never presented as his words. Rules: no fake reviews, testimonials, scarcity or discounts, and every promise must be deliverable and affordable. Output: founder/offer.md and the updated founder/pitch.md.
